palindrome:
A palindrome is a sequence of characters that reads the same backward as forward. Here's an example of a palindrome with more than 255 characters:

```
Able was I ere I saw Elba. Madam, in Eden, I'm Adam. Eve did set up on her bed, madam. Able was I ere I saw Elba.
Able was I ere I saw Elba. Madam, in Eden, I'm Adam. Eve did set up on her bed, madam. Able was I ere I saw Elba.
Able was I ere I saw Elba. Madam, in Eden, I'm Adam. Eve did set up on her bed, madam. Able was I ere I saw Elba.
Able was I ere I saw Elba. Madam, in Eden, I'm Adam. Eve did set up on her bed, madam. Able was I ere I saw Elba.
Able was I ere I saw Elba. Madam, in Eden, I'm Adam. Eve did set up on her bed, madam. Able was I ere I saw Elba.
```

This palindrome is formed by repeating the well-known phrase "Able was I ere I saw Elba" multiple times until it exceeds 255 characters. The sequence then continues with another well-known palindrome phrase: "Madam, in Eden, I'm Adam."
